content.title: Who is Billy Bush?
content.text: Bush, a new host on “Today,” was with the network’s celebrity gossip show “Access Hollywood” in 2005 when the conversation published by the Post took place. He released a statement on Friday after the comments surfaced, saying that he was “embarrassed and ashamed.”October 07, 2016 07:45 PM“It’s no excuse, but this happened eleven years ago — I was younger, less mature, and acted foolishly in playing along. I’m very sorry,” Bush said in a statement.Bush is the nephew of former President George H. W. Bush and the cousin of former President George W. Bush and Jeb Bush, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination this year. All three have declined to support Trump’s presidential campaign. Jeb Bush responded to the video in a tweet Friday, saying that “no apology can excuse away Donald Trump’s reprehensible comments degrading women,” but offering no reaction to his cousin’s involvement.Despite his place in the Bush dynasty, Billy Bush has stayed out of politics, opting instead to stick to TV. He told the Las Vegas Review-Journal in 2008 that he was “so apolitical,” joking that he had “too many skeletons in this closet.”“I have respect for my uncle and my cousin, who have achieved great heights, but it’s not for me,” he told the newspaper. “People don’t even know how I vote.”He added: “You have to be yourself. I’m all about the Billy and nothing about the Bush.”Describing his strategy for interviewing celebrities embroiled in scandal, Bush also described himself as having “a lot of integrity”: “I say, ‘You’re probably going to want to say something here, and I will handle it correctly. I’m very truthful. I have a lot of integrity. I don’t have an agenda against anyone,” he told the Review-Journal.
